title: Cabinet door templates
description: Routing templates for the curved rails and stiles of an inset cabinet door. The split templates join together so you can print a full-length routing guide on a smaller printer.
license: No license declared; see project provenance.

views.label: Full template
views.notes: V10 retains the approved V9 dovetail. Full-template strength remains untested. Use the V9 rail fit coupon for this joint.
views.print: Use the arranged Bambu project. Keep the two halves from this revision together.
views.description: A routing guide for the curved horizontal rails of an inset cabinet door. Join the two printed halves with their matching dovetail to make the full template. Use both halves from this revision together.

views.label: Fit coupon
views.notes: The V9 coupon fit was approved. Rail V10 preserves this joint. This coupon is for the rail; it is not compatible with the V13 stile joint.
views.print: Two pieces, printed flat. The existing slice reports 23 min and 13.59 g, without supports. Check the printer and material before using a sliced project.
views.description: A small two-piece sample of the rail template’s dovetail joint. Print it to check how the halves slide together before making the full rail template. This joint matches Rail V10.

views.label: Full template
views.notes: The user reports that the full V13 joint is too tight and bows the socket arms. The earlier V12 .05 coupon passed, but that result did not transfer to the full print. Cause under investigation.
views.print: Hold further V13 full-stile prints while the fit failure is investigated. Existing files are retained for reference.
views.description: A routing guide for the vertical side of the inset cabinet door, printed in two halves that join with a dovetail. The current V13 joint is too tight and bends the socket arms, so wait for a corrected version before printing the full template.

views.label: Fit coupon
views.notes: Cut directly from the full V13 halves. Mating geometry matches the previously successful V12 .05 coupon, but the full V13 print was subsequently reported too tight with bowed socket arms. This coupon result does not validate the full print.
views.print: Two coupon pieces arranged for the P1S. The recorded slice is about 28 min and 17.5 g.
views.status: V12 coupon passed · full print failed
views.description: A short sample of the V13 stile template’s dovetail joint. Use it to check the connection with less material than a full template. The full V13 template has a reported tight-fit problem, even though an earlier small sample fit well.

title: Sanding plane
description: A hand sanding plane for the curved face of a board shaped with the Magnate 5869 fingernail router bit. The rear handle gives you a grip while the shaped shoe supports the sandpaper against the curve. Slide the shoe into the body and hand-tighten the front knob to hold it in place; loosen the knob to swap shoes.

views.label: Assembly
views.print: P1S · PLA · 0.4 mm nozzle · 0.20 mm layers · 5 walls · 15% infill. Carrier side-down with supports; shoe rail-cap-down/profile-up and knob crown-down without supports. Use the configured Bambu project.
views.notes: Tapered coupon passed a physical test without shifting. Full-size loading and long-term wear remain untested.

title: Eighth-circle stencil
description: A drawing stencil for laying out curved furniture parts on paper. Set the rounded corner at the center of your circle, then trace the edge beside the radius you want. The labeled edges cover 1 to 10 inches in half-inch steps.
notes: Ready for a first test print. Use light pencil pressure along the curved edges. Let the long, thin rails cool before removal.
print: PLA · 0.20 mm layers · 0.4 mm nozzle · 3 walls · no supports. Keep the stencil flat on the bed at 100% scale.
license: No license declared; see project provenance.

title: Fingernail-profile caul
description: A shaped clamping block for gluing veneer onto the curved face of a board cut with the Magnate 5869 fingernail router bit. Place a 2×4 along its flat back to spread clamp pressure over the veneer. Cover the contact face with packing tape to keep glue from sticking to it.
notes: CAD and mesh dimensions are verified. Physical fit against the routed board still needs checking. The 2×4 supplies stiffness along the length.
print: Flat clamp face on the bed, no supports. 4 walls and 15–20% infill for the thin backed version. Disable brims that exceed the bed.
license: No license declared; see project provenance.

print: Starting point: 0.20 mm layers, 0.4 mm nozzle, 3 walls, no supports. Use the supplied print orientation.

title: Cardboard can
description: Turn the cardboard core from a Bambu filament spool into a stackable storage container. The printed lid, ring, and bottom fit around the core, with dividers for smaller items. Line up the notch in the cardboard with the nub inside the ring when assembling it.
license: Embedded box attribution: sdaendi; print profile: JSBG. Embedded license: Standard Digital File License. The original MakerWorld terms apply.
related: Organizer for recyclable cardboard spool box
print: Open the complete two-plate project in Bambu Studio. Saved settings: Bambu Lab P1S, 0.4 mm nozzle, Generic PLA, 0.20 mm layers, 3 walls, 15% infill, supports disabled. Use the cardboard core from a Bambu filament spool; align its notch with the nub in the printed ring.
notes: The saved 3MF archive passed its integrity check. Previews use its plate membership, object geometry, and build transforms. Physical fit and print results are undocumented.
